artists.biography:
Nelson is an American rock band founded by singer/songwriters Matthew and Gunnar Nelson (twin sons of Ricky Nelson and Kristin Nelson). The band achieved huge success during the early 90s with their debut album After the Rain. The album featured the No. 1 hit "(Can't Live Without Your) Love and Affection" and also reached multi-platinum status.

After the success of their first album, the band claims to have been faced with conflicts with their record label, lack of support from the media, and the shift in music towards grunge and alternative rock. They eventually split with Geffen Records in 1995. Despite this, the band has continued to produce and release albums independently under their own label, Stone Canyon Records.

Matthew and Gunnar also perform under the name of Ricky Nelson Remembered, as a tribute to their father. They are listed in the Guinness Book of World Records as the only family to reach number one record status in three successive generations (beginning with grandparents Ozzie and Harriet Nelson).

perplexity.description:
After the Rain is the debut studio album by American rock duo Nelson, released on June 26, 1990, through DGC Records. Musically, the album blends melodic hard rock with pop sensibilities, featuring polished guitar riffs, strong vocal harmonies, and catchy hooks that defined the early 1990s rock sound. The album is best known for its chart-topping single "(Can't Live Without Your) Love and Affection," which reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became a gold-certified hit. Other notable tracks include "After the Rain" and "Only Time Will Tell," both of which also charted in the Top 10 and Top 40, respectively.

As Nelson's breakthrough release, After the Rain marked the duo's arrival on the mainstream rock scene and remains their most commercially successful album. It peaked at #17 on the Billboard 200 and spent 64 weeks on the chart, eventually earning double platinum certification from the RIAA for sales exceeding two million copies. The album's success led to a massive world tour and established Nelson as prominent figures in the glam and melodic rock genres of the era. While subsequent releases did not match its impact, After the Rain stands as a defining work in the band's discography and a notable example of early 1990s rock.
